'''Chia-Kun (John) Chu''' ({{zh|c=朱家琨|p=Zhū Jiākūn}}; August 14, 1927 – January 2, 2023) was a Chinese-American applied mathematician who was the Fu Foundation Professor Emeritus of Applied Mathematics at [[Columbia University]]. He had been on Columbia faculty since 1965 and served as the department chairman of applied physics and nuclear engineering three times (1982–1983, 1985–1988, 1995–1997).<ref name="C.K.Chu Profile">{{cite web|url=http://apam.columbia.edu/ck-chu |title=Prof C.K. Chu at Applied Physics and Applied Mathematics Columbia University|date=11 July 2019}}</ref>

==Biography==
Chu received a bachelor's in mechanical engineering from [[Shanghai Jiao Tong University|Chiao-Tung University]] in 1948, a master's from [[Cornell University]] in 1950, and a Ph.D. from [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences|Courant Institute]], [[New York University]] in 1959.<ref name="C.K.Chu Profile"/>

Chu was an internationally recognized applied mathematician and one of the pioneers of computational mathematics in fluid dynamics, magnetohydrodynamics, and shock waves. He developed approximations to the differential equations of fluid dynamics and coined the term "computational fluid dynamics".<ref name="C.K.Chu Honored">{{cite web|url=http://sites.apam.columbia.edu/newsevents/chu_honorary_degree.html |title=Columbia News May 17, 2006}}</ref>

Chu received numerous honors. He was a recipient of [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] and was elected fellow of [[American Physical Society]] and fellow of [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]]. He was awarded an honorary Doctor of Science degree from [[Columbia University]] in 2006.<ref name="C.K.Chu Profile"/><ref name="C.K.Chu Honored"/>

Chia-Kun Chu was the son of bank chairman Ju Tang Chu.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/02/26/business/ju-tang-chu-97-chinese-banks-ex-head.html|title = Ju Tang Chu, 97, Chinese Banks' Ex-Head|newspaper = The New York Times|date = February 26, 1998|page=B11|access-date=November 7, 2022}}</ref> Chia-Kun Chu was also the brother-in-law of [[Fu Zaiyuan]], a Columbia donor who gave his name for the [[Fu Foundation School of Engineering and Applied Science]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1997/10/01/us/chinese-tycoon-gives-columbia-26-million.html|title = Chinese Tycoon Gives Columbia $26 Million|newspaper = The New York Times|date = October 1997|last1 = Arenson|first1 = Karen W.}}</ref>

Chia-Kun Chu died on January 2, 2023, at the age of 95.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chia-Kun Chu |url=https://www.tributearchive.com/obituaries/26945917/chia-kun-chu |website=Tribute Archive |access-date=11 October 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=C.K. Chu (1927–2023) |url=https://www.engineering.columbia.edu/ck-chu-1927-2023 |website=Columbia University in the City of New York |access-date=11 October 2023}}</ref>
